claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2 text adds the round-1 condition ("when the code that calls or implements an interface needs different parts of it, split it"). Pinned docs frame ISP per dependent: "Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." (options.md:12). The unconditional ranking is gone; the split is now conditional and consistent with section 6.

"A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." (interfaces.md:86). Lesson now says "apart from any the interface gives a body of its own", matching the exception. CS0535 fix: "Provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface, or declare the type as abstract" (interface-implementation-errors.md:140).

Unchanged from round 1. Execution (SDK 10, net10.0): implementer keeping GetDeliveryReport(int) after the interface changed to GetDeliveryReport(int, bool) gave "error CS0535: 'Sms' does not implement interface member 'IChannel.GetDeliveryReport(int, bool)'". Doc: "The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (interfaces.md:35).
git show stage-0:.../INotifier.cs lines 5-8: `public interface INotifier { void Send(int orderId, string subject); }` - one member. Code block lines=5-8 matches character-for-character.

git show stage-0: line 5 `public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier`; line 7 private `List<string> sent`; line 9 `IReadOnlyList<string> Sent => sent`; lines 11-16 Send calls Format, sent.Add, Console.WriteLine; line 18 `protected abstract string Format(...)`; lines 21-31 EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier override only Format. Code block lines=21-31 matches.

`git -C examples/don-hang grep -n -i deliver stage-0 -- samples` returns no lines. No INotificationChannel or GetDeliveryReport at stage-0. `git grep -i confirm stage-0` and `stage-1` also return nothing, so the confirmation code is not in the samples either.

"C# doesn't have the concept of checked exceptions. Any method might (in theory) throw any exception." (tips-for-java-developers.md:16) - nothing in the interface signature tells a caller that one implementation throws. The LSP link restates the prerequisite lesson.
Design judgement restating outline misconception 2, not a version-dependent fact. Consistent with the pinned per-dependent framing of ISP (options.md:12), which says nothing about member count.

Doc: implicit reference conversion when "assigning a reference type instance to a variable of an interface the type implements" (conversions.md:46). Execution (SDK 10, stage-0 INotifier.cs + NotifierBase.cs copied verbatim): `INotifier[] all = { new EmailNotifier(), new SmsNotifier() }; foreach (INotifier n in all) n.Send(7, "placed");` builds and prints "email about order 7: placed" / "sms about order 7: placed".

Only a type that implements the interface converts to it (conversions.md:46), and implementing requires every member without a default body (interfaces.md:86). Execution (SDK 10): passing `new SmsOnly()` (has SendSms only) to `Use(IChannel c)` with IChannel{SendEmail; SendSms} gives "error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'SmsOnly' to 'IChannel'".

issues.text: "yet" implies the confirmation code will be added to the samples later. `git grep -i confirm` finds nothing at stage-0 or stage-1, and no outline in content/tracks/*/track.yaml mentions confirmation code. The promise is unbacked.
issues.quote: code that sends an order confirmation — not in the samples yet — would call only one of the four
issues.fix: Replace "not in the samples yet" with "imagined for this lesson" (or "not in the samples").

issues.text: q6 fill: answer set accepts only "INotifier" (case-insensitive, trimmed). The namespace-qualified name "DonHang.Samples.Oop.INotifier", which is also correct, and a backticked "`INotifier`" are both rejected.

The arrows mean two different things: F --> S is 'implemented by', F --> C is 'used by', and I --> E / I --> M skip NotifierBase. The section 4 prose never mentions EmailNotifier or SmsNotifier under INotifier; I only learn how they relate in section 5. I cannot narrate the right half of the diagram after reading section 4.
issues.fix: In the third paragraph of section 4, add one sentence: "On the right of the diagram, EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier each implement INotifier (through NotifierBase) and have real behaviour for its one method." Also add one clause saying the left arrows show who implements and who calls the fat interface.

issues.text: The paragraph is announced as the calling side, but its concrete consequence (a GetDeliveryReport change forces SmsNotifier to change) is about implementers. I cannot see what actually goes wrong for the confirmation code, and I half-conclude the confirmation code must change too. The caller-side harm only appears later, in section 6.
issues.quote: If someone changes the parameters of `GetDeliveryReport`, every class that implements the interface has to change, including `SmsNotifier`
issues.fix: Move the GetDeliveryReport sentence to the implementing-side paragraph, and give the calling-side paragraph its own concrete cost, e.g. one sentence: a class that only sends SMS cannot be passed to the confirmation code unless it adds filler for the other three.

issues.text: The misconception as written can be read as 'every implementing class uses every method', which would not be a fat interface at all, so the belief seems harmless and I cannot see what is wrong with it. Quiz q2 states the intended belief more clearly ('each of its methods is used by some class in the system').
issues.quote: A big interface is fine as long as every class implementing it eventually uses every method somewhere.
issues.fix: Reword the belief to match q2: "A big interface is fine as long as each of its methods is used by some class somewhere in the system."

issues.text: 'without a body of its own' made me stop: the five-line summaries only say an interface says what callers may call, so an interface method having a body is a new idea here. I re-read the sentence twice. Same phrase in q1's correct explanation ('without a default body').
issues.quote: C# requires a class to provide every method the interface declares without a body of its own, which is all four here.
issues.fix: Add a short reminder in the same sentence: "(C# lets an interface give a method a default body; none of these four has one)".

issues.text: 'The code that sends an order confirmation' is used throughout (diagram, try it, quiz) but never tied to anything in the samples. I know PlaceOrderSplit.Notify from earlier lessons and cannot tell whether this is it or a hypothetical.
issues.quote: And the code that sends an order confirmation calls only one of the four, yet now depends on all of them.
issues.fix: Add a few words saying whether this is PlaceOrderSplit.Notify or an imagined piece of code, e.g. "the code that sends an order confirmation (imagined for this lesson)".

issues.text: 'users' could mean people using the app; here it means code that calls or implements the interface. I had to check which one.
issues.quote: ISP's answer is to cut interfaces along what their users need.
issues.fix: Replace "their users" with "the code that calls or implements them".

issues.text: q2: correct option c is nearly a verbatim sentence from section 6 ('ISP asks about each piece of code that depends on the interface, not about the system as a whole'), so it can be matched without understanding.
issues.quote: False, because ISP asks about each caller and implementer, not the system as a whole.
issues.fix: Rephrase option c in new words, e.g. "False, because the confirmation code still needs channels that carry all four methods, even if other code uses them."

issues.text: q4: correct option a is the longest and the only one using the lesson's term 'fat interface'; I can pick it from wording alone.
issues.quote: The fat interface forced `SmsNotifier` to promise `SendEmail`, which it could only fill with a throw.
issues.fix: Shorten option a to similar length as the others and drop the term, e.g. "The interface made `SmsNotifier` promise an email it cannot send."

issues.text: q6: the blank is filled by copying the Core concepts sentence word for word; it tests recall of wording, not understanding.
issues.quote: ISP: no code should be forced to depend on methods it does not ____.
issues.fix: Blank a word that needs understanding, e.g. "When SmsNotifier must write bodies for SendEmail and SendPush, those bodies are called ____." (answer: filler).
